newsitem.title: CANADA: HORSE RACING-CIGAR, DARE AND GO SAID READY TO BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CIGAR, DARE AND GO SAID READY TO BATTLE.

text.p: Superstar Cigar seemed to be in top condition Friday with a strong 1-1/4-mile gallop around the Woodbine track a day before the six-year-old likely will end one of the greatest careers in history.

"He was moving well, handling the track fine. He's awfully sharp, awfully good," said Cigar's trainer Bill Mott of the defending champion in Saturday's Breeders' Cup Classic over the same distance he ran Friday.

Richard Mandella, the trainer of Dare and Go, who at 6-1 is expected to be Cigar's toughest opponent in the Classic, was not quite as effusive in rating the condition of his horse, part of an entry with the weaker Atticus.

But he did say "as far as we can see he looks good and we think he is in the same shape as before the Pacific Classic," a reference to the race last August when Dare and Go halted Cigar's consecutive victory streak at 16 for a tie with the great Citation for the modern-day record.
Mott was very aware of the pressures that come with success.

Cigar has "been so good on so many occasions -- in his last 20 races -- there's been no time that he's not been good," Mott said. "He's probably set very high standards for himself, and people have come to expect nothing less than what he's done before. That's tough to repeat over a 20-race period."

Cigar, who has won 17 of his last 19 races, was set as the 4-5 favourite Wednesday after drawing the seventh post position for the $4 million race, which has a first-place prize of $2, 080,000. Second place is worth $800,000 and third $480,000.
Yanks Music, the three-year-old filly who will try to shatter the glass ceiling in the Classic, "went pretty quick" in her three furlong workout Friday, said trainer Leo O'Brien.
"She's ready to run. She was acting like she was wanting to roll this morning. She has no problem with the track."

Asked if the 35-2/5 seconds time for his filly was too fast the day before the big race, O'Brien said: "A little bit slower work would have been better maybe. With all the excitement going on, she was well wound up when she worked. She was aggressive. But better to be aggressive than to be too quiet.
Preakness Stakes winner Louis Quatorze, set at 12-1 after drawing the 11th gate, galloped 1-3/8 miles on Friday's beautifully crisp fall day.
His trainer, Nick Zito, showed his typically reserved and honest approach to his charges.
Zito said his horse was well-adjusted to the track, "but he was last time, too," the trainer said, referring to the colt's trip north for a disappointing seventh-place here September 15.
"I know it's not the track (that caused the bad showing). Maybe it was the surroundings or the long walk to the track."
Mahogany Hall's trainer, Jim Baker, was asked which horse he would like to run in the Classic if he could not have Mahogany Hall, a 20-1 early-line pick.
"If I can have anybody, I'd like Secretariat," Baker said. "But of the horses in the race it would be Cigar because he has that tactical speed to be anywhere you want him to be."
